solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Gary's award picked up for construction

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the phrase is said aloud and its sound gives the entry

parts.note: Gaz is a familiar short form of Gary, and his award is an OBE, so this is Gaz OBE

explanation.surface: Someone called Gary receives a prize for a building project.
explanation.walkthrough: OBE is the Order of the British Empire, a UK honour. 'Gaz OBE' said aloud matches the entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden summerhouse with a view is a small structure, so it counts as a construction.

clue.text: Fatal result of further discussion being repeatedly curtailed

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short at the tail; repeatedly says both words lose their final letter

parts.note: further can mean more, as in further reasons
talk is discussion

explanation.surface: Endless debate keeps being cut short, with deadly results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly curtailed' docks both MORE and TALK, leaving MOR and TAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A mortal wound is a fatal one: synonyms meaning causing death.

clue.text: Martin perhaps drafted fine novel around about now?

indicators.note: around about says the rearranged letters are placed round the outside of the next piece
novel means new or fresh, so these letters are given a fresh arrangement

parts.note: here and now: here means at this point, now

explanation.surface: A writer has drafted a fine novel, apparently set round about the present day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' signals rearranging DRAFTED FINE, and 'around about' wraps that result round the word for now. 'Martin' looks like a person's name but is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A house martin is a bird, and a bird is jocularly called this; 'perhaps' marks an example.

clue.text: Language that can be followed by setter, 20, in translation

definitions.text: Language that can be followed by setter

indicators.note: translation changes the form of the words, so the letters of the cross-referenced answer are rearranged

parts.note: 20 refers to the answer to clue 20, SHINGLE, meaning gravel

explanation.surface: A setter talks of some language that can follow, with a cross-reference translated.
explanation.walkthrough: The English setter is a breed of gundog, so the language name can be followed by 'setter'. The comma before '20' misleads: it is the anagram fodder, not an aside.
explanation.definitionFit: The tongue of Britain is a language, and placed before setter it names a dog breed.

clue.text: Make the front cover of Punch with article on principal policies

parts.note: to punch is to hit
the is the definite article
a principal of a school is its head
a line is a policy or course, as in the party line

explanation.surface: A satirical magazine's cover deals with an article on leading policies.
explanation.walkthrough: Punch was a British humour magazine, which makes 'front cover of Punch' read as one phrase; 'of' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: getting front-page news coverage means appearing on the cover of a paper.

clue.text: Journalist hacking Soviet sportsman

indicators.note: hacking means cutting into, so the journalist's letters cut into the Soviet's

parts.note: Russki is a slang word for a Russian or Soviet person
ED, short for editor, is a common crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter is attacking a Soviet athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: Greg Rusedski was a British tennis player of the 1990s and 2000s.
explanation.definitionFit: Greg Rusedski was a professional tennis player, so a sportsman by example.

clue.text: Space by one-line poem?

parts.note: uni- is the prefix meaning one
a verse is a line of a poem, or poetry generally

explanation.surface: Something placed beside a single-line poem, puzzlingly.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke: a poem of one line would be a uni-verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Outer space and the cosmos are synonyms for everything that exists.

clue.text: Emperor's new guard cut by half in a long time

indicators.note: in places the shortened guard inside the long time

parts.note: an aeon is a very long time

indicators.note: cut by half means only the first three of six letters are kept

parts.note: the police guard the public

explanation.surface: An emperor's newly formed guard is reduced by half over a long period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut by half' keeps the first half of the six-letter guard; 'in' then places it within the long time, after the abbreviation for new.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon Bonaparte was Emperor of the French; the possessive is read as 'Emperor is'.

clue.text: Antigua naturally provides habitat for a creature

indicators.note: provides habitat for says the creature lives inside these two words

explanation.surface: A Caribbean island is a natural home for a particular animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The iguana is a large tropical lizard, an example of a creature.

clue.text: Corporation formed by good German

definitions.meaning: corporation is an old jocular word for a large belly

explanation.surface: A company was set up by a decent German.
explanation.definitionFit: A corporation in old slang is a paunch, and paunch and belly are synonyms.

clue.text: Support complete drunk? No way

parts.note: a tee supports a golf ball
total means complete, as in a total failure

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a supporter is completely drunk, and is told certainly not.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who never touches alcohol is never drunk: the definition is a description, not a synonym.

clue.text: Live on and off in quaint housing that's left here?

indicators.note: housing means holding inside, so the quaint word contains the other letters

parts.note: twee means quaint or overly cute

indicators.note: on and off means taking every other letter of live

explanation.surface: Living intermittently in a cute house, with a hint about what's left.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition refers to the clue's own number, printed just to the left of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: This clue is numbered with the number in question, which sits on the left of the clue.

clue.text: Rustle poem up, a certain rhyming couplet

indicators.note: up means stirred up or in disorder, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: sure means certain

explanation.surface: A poem is rustled up, featuring a certain rhyming couplet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' signals rearranging RUSTLE POEM; 'Rustle' looks like the verb of the surface but is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Poulter's measure is a metre of alternating twelve- and fourteen-syllable lines, used in pairs.

clue.text: Regularly surpass successes

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at regular intervals, here every second one

explanation.surface: Someone routinely outdoes previous achievements.
explanation.definitionFit: Ups, as in ups and downs, are good times or successes.

clue.text: House doctors needing books lost lives

indicators.note: lost says these letters go missing from the doctors

parts.note: hospital doctors who live in are house doctors or residents
NT is the New Testament, books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Junior hospital doctors who need textbooks have lost lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' is read as the deletion signal, not as a verb with 'lives' as its object.
explanation.definitionFit: To live somewhere is to reside there: synonyms for dwelling.

clue.text: Computer system that links two numbers, one reversed

parts.note: ether is a number in the sense of something that numbs, an anaesthetic

indicators.note: reversed says the second number is written backwards

parts.note: one of the two numbers is ten

explanation.surface: A computer network connects two figures, one of them backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'numbers' is the old crossword trick: a numb-er, an anaesthetic. 'two numbers' then shares out as ETHER and TEN, the latter 'reversed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethernet is the standard wired networking technology connecting computers.

clue.text: When short, mean workers bust up thanks to these

indicators.note: short means missing the end, so the word for mean loses its last letter

parts.note: to imply is to mean
worker ants make ants classic crossword workers

explanation.surface: Stingy staff, in short, start a fight because of these.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust up' seems to mean a quarrel, but it is a bust made bigger by breast enhancements.
explanation.definitionFit: Breast implants enlarge the bust, so a bust goes up thanks to them.

clue.text: Wants fathers to go on dole after vacation

indicators.note: to go on means to be attached after, so the fathers follow
after vacation means emptied of its middle, leaving the outer letters

parts.note: to sire is to father, so sires are fathers

explanation.surface: Fathers want to go on the dole after their holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacation' looks like a holiday but signals emptying DOLE to DE.
explanation.definitionFit: Wants and desires are synonyms as plural nouns, or as verbs.

clue.text: Grass snake, usually bolder, finally retreats

indicators.note: retreats means going backwards, so the letters are read in the opposite order
finally means the last letter of each word

explanation.surface: A snake that is normally braver ends up backing off.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye is a cereal plant, and cereals are a kind of grass.

clue.text: One holding hot gravel

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the word for one surrounds the other letter

parts.note: single means one
H is the standard abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A single person is holding hot gravel.
explanation.definitionFit: Shingle is beach gravel of small rounded stones.

clue.text: Fish, he protested, may evolve into an apparently marine creature

indicators.note: may evolve means may change form, so the letters of the fish and the protest are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man protests that a fish might evolve into a sea creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apparently marine' fits because the creature is a camel, called a ship only by metaphor.
explanation.definitionFit: The camel is nicknamed for crossing sand as a vessel crosses sea, so it seems marine.

clue.text: Lewdness discovered around country

indicators.note: around means turned about, so the remaining letters are rearranged
discovered means with the covering removed, so the outer letters go

explanation.surface: Indecency was found across a whole nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered' strips LEWDNESS to EWDNES, and 'around' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweden is a Scandinavian nation, an example of a country.

clue.text: Change sides with brown switch

parts.note: to rat is to desert to the other side
tan is a brown colour

explanation.surface: Someone changes sides with a brown light switch.
explanation.definitionFit: A rattan is a cane, and a switch is a thin flexible cane or stick.

clue.text: Panic when copper goes after weapon designer

indicators.note: after places the shortened panic behind the weapon

parts.note: an arm is a weapon

indicators.note: goes means leaves, so the policeman's letters are taken out of panic

parts.note: PC, police constable, is a British copper

explanation.surface: Someone panics as a policeman pursues a weapons designer.
explanation.walkthrough: The P and C removed are not side by side: they are the first and last letters of PANIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Giorgio Armani is a famous Italian fashion designer.

clue.text: Sweet sound, note, on time

parts.note: noise is sound
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A pleasing sound, a note held right on the beat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' looks like it describes the sound, but it is the noun: a confection.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisette is a hazelnut chocolate, a kind of sweet.

clue.text: Ultimately, the big bang is explosive

definitions.note: a noun here: an explosive device; slang for a bomb or grenade

indicators.note: ultimately means last, so the final letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: In the end, the Big Bang was explosive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link. 'explosive' looks like an adjective but is a noun: a bomb, egg in military slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Military slang calls a bomb or grenade an egg, so it is an explosive.

clue.text: She helped us to cook food in advance

parts.note: beet is a vegetable, a food
on means ahead or forward, as in getting on

explanation.surface: A woman helped by cooking food beforehand.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Beeton wrote a famous Victorian British cookery and household book.
explanation.definitionFit: Isabella Beeton's book taught generations of cooks, so she helped people to cook.

clue.text: Story with good title about subject

parts.note: a story can be a lie

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for title is read backwards

parts.note: a title is a name

explanation.surface: A tale with a good title about a theme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'subject' looks like a topic, but here it is a person subject to a lord.
explanation.definitionFit: A liegeman was a feudal vassal, a subject owing allegiance to a lord.
